en: The Jātaka:
Catukkanipāta, Kāliṅgavagga (The Chapter on Kāliṅga)
1. The Cūḷakāliṅga Jātaka: “Open this gate;
let the city be entered by King Aruṇa.”
By Sīha the well-bred,
by Surakkhita, and by Nandisena.
Victory to the Kalingas, who are difficult to overcome!
"Defeat and misfortune have come upon the Assakas;
thus indeed was it spoken by you, O practitioner of the holy life.
Those who have become upright do not speak what is false."
“O Sakka, among the gods who have transcended false speech,
truth is their supreme wealth. Therefore,
O King of Gods, that which you have spoken is a falsehood.”
“On what basis do you say ‘Maghavan’ and ‘Mahinda’?
“Have you not heard, O Brahmin, while it was being recited:
‘The gods do not equal the prowess of a man’?”
The concentration of the mind is unshakable,
non-distraction and timely exertion,
firm energy, and human endeavor.
"By that very means, there was victory in the Assaka forest.
Thus ends the first Cūḷakāliṅga Jātaka.
